issues.description: The problem text (Part 2) specifies messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (i.e., a method that takes a double parameter and includes the volume in the returned string), but the UML, the provided template usage, and the solution all define messageOnMilk() with no parameters and return a simple string (e.g., "Seal Clarabelle is milked"). This parameter mismatch is contradictory and will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and what the tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either (A) update the problem text to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and specify the return format like the UML/solution (e.g., "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), or (B) change the interfaces, template usage, and solution to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update tests and example code accordingly. Preferred fix: align the textual description to the UML and solution by removing the double parameter and describing the no-argument messageOnMilk() return value.

issues.description: The problem text specifies a method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) that includes a milkVolume parameter and requests the returned string to include the volume, while the UML diagram, the template Main usage, and the solution implementation define/use a no-argument messageOnMilk() returning a simple milking message. This mismatch between the problem description and the provided/template/solution code creates a direct signature and behavioral inconsistency: students will be uncertain whether to implement a parameterized method (and how to call it) or a no-argument method, and whether the returned string must include the volume.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the problem description to require a no-argument messageOnMilk() that returns the milking message (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked") to match the UML/template/solution; or (B) change the interface and all implementations (Milkable, Seal, Goat, and any calls in Main/Farm) to messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update example return strings to include the volume (e.g. "Seal Clarabelle is milked (volume: 1.5L)"). Recommended: adopt option (A) to align with the existing UML and template code and avoid forcing parameter changes in many places.
